chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text:
I think #3576 didn't quite capture my concern.  Specifically, eMudhra is an example of where I'm worried our warnings and mitigations in Impersonation are adequate:

This mechanism could increase the impact of a key compromise. Rather than needing to subvert DNS or IP routing in order to use a compromised certificate, a malicious server now only needs a client to connect to some HTTPS site under its control in order to present the compromised certificate. Clients SHOULD consult DNS for hostnames presented in secondary certificates if they would have done so for the same hostname if it were present in the primary certificate.

ie, with the combination Seconday Certs (+ORIGIN) it becomes far easier to get clients to establish connections to a compromised/impersonated site in the case of a CA or Intermediate compromise.
I'm not sure how we effectively defend against this -- not everyone is as good as the major browsers in responding to Intermediate CA compromise.
